name: The five faults of calm abiding
description: Laziness, forgetting the instruction, sinking and agitation, non-application (of the remedy) and over-application (applying it when not needed) — the obstacles to stability of mind.

name: Sinking (laya)
description: Yogācāra contribution: the sinking of the mind in calm abiding, to be noticed by awareness and remedied by lifting the mind; one of the five faults.

name: Distraction (vikṣepa)
description: Yogācāra contribution: the mind straying from its object, to be noticed quickly and brought back (MSA 14.11); the Madhyāntavibhāga lists kinds of distraction (emerging, toward objects, relishing sinking and agitation, expectation, (hidden) intention, self-conceit in attention, lower mind).
notes: The Madhyāntavibhāga list is paraphrased from 5.12–13 (checked in the e-text) without the bhāṣya's glosses.

name: The afflictive and cognitive obscurations
description: Yogācāra contribution: all obscurations are summed up as the afflictive obscuration (removed by the selflessness of persons) and the cognitive obscuration (removed by the selflessness of dharmas); liberation follows their exhaustion.

name: The four afflictions of the afflicted mind
description: Self-view, self-delusion, self-conceit and self-love, which always accompany the seventh consciousness.

name: The six root afflictions (Yogācāra)
description: Greed, aversion, delusion, conceit, (wrong) views and doubt.

name: The twenty secondary afflictions
description: Anger, enmity, concealment, spite, envy, avarice, deceit, dishonesty, pride, harmfulness, shamelessness, non-embarrassment, torpor, agitation, lack of faith, laziness, heedlessness, forgetfulness, distraction and non-awareness.

name: The nine fetters
description: Yogācāra contribution: the Madhyāntavibhāga (2.1–3) names the nine fetters as the characteristic of affliction — attraction, aversion, pride, ignorance, views, holding to the supreme, doubt, envy and avarice.

name: Badness, unwieldiness (dauṣṭhulya)
description: The heaviness and unworkability of body and mind, the substrate of defilement; removed in part by pliancy in meditation and wholly by the transformation of the basis.

name: The four dangers to the lineage
description: Habituation to the afflictions, bad friends, deprivation, and dependence on others — which keep one with the bodhisattva lineage from awakening.

name: The ten undefiled ignorances regarding the dharmadhātu
description: Ten non-afflicted ignorances concerning ten aspects of the dharmadhātu (its all-pervasiveness, supremacy etc.), whose antidotes are the ten grounds.
notes: Checked that MAV 2.16 names 'this undefiled tenfold ignorance regarding the dharmadhātu' with the grounds as antidotes; the list is in 2.14–15.

name: Self-grasping as the root of faults
description: Seeing a self produces love for it, thirst for happiness, appropriation of means as 'mine', the division of self and other, clinging and aversion, and all faults; as long as it lasts one is in saṃsāra.
